causes.text: In a note released on Jan. 19 2022, Vanda Research analysts said individual investors were buying far less than usual during market sell-offs, indicating fatigue after the previous year's tech-fuelled trading frenzy. The report noted that enthusiasm for meme stocks was fading and Gen Z investors were shifting attention to sectors like electric vehicles and the metaverse.

source_info.title: Retail investors show signs of fatigue after last year's trading frenzy - report

effects.text: Reuters reported on Apr. 28 2022 that Robinhood's first-quarter revenue fell 43 % and monthly active users dropped year on year. The trading slowdown led investors to push the stock more than 12 % lower after hours.

source_info.title: Robinhood shares tumble after revenue drops 43% and user growth stalls

causal_reasoning_chain.description: On 2022-01-19, Vanda Research highlighted that retail investors were showing fatigue after 2021's meme-stock boom, buying significantly less during market sell-offs and turning their attention away from meme stocks.
This decline in retail trading enthusiasm led to lower transaction volumes at commission-free brokers like Robinhood, reducing fee and order-flow revenues over the subsequent months.
Consequently, when Robinhood released its first-quarter results on 2022-04-28, it reported a 43 % revenue drop and fewer active users, causing its shares to fall more than 12 % after hours.

rationale: The effect article attributes Robinhood's sharp revenue decline to reduced trading volumes, which aligns with the earlier report showing that retail investors were buying less and losing interest in meme stocks. Reduced activity directly diminishes transaction revenue.
counterfactual_analysis: Had retail investors maintained the frenetic trading pace seen in 2021, Robinhood's revenue would likely have been higher, and its share price might not have dropped as sharply when the results were announced.

adversarial_confounders.text: Rising interest rates and high inflation could have also discouraged trading and reduced spending power, contributing to the revenue drop independently of retail fatigue.
adversarial_confounders.impact: Macro-economic pressures may partially confound the link by simultaneously reducing retail trading and directly hurting financial stocks.

details.commentary: Signs that retail traders are pulling back mean that Robinhood must fight harder with other brokers and apps for a smaller pool of active customers. As volumes and meme stock activity fade, its transaction driven model looks more fragile compared with competitors that earn steadier fee or interest income.

details.pestel_factor: Political - Regulatory and market oversight pressures
details.commentary: After the pandemic, higher living costs and changing risk appetites led many small investors to reduce speculative trading. That social and economic shift weakened the tailwind that had powered Robinhood's rapid growth, making a steep revenue decline and user stagnation more likely.
